results.title: What being a female startup founder in UK is like | London vs SF, Fundraising, Imposter Syndrome
results.snippet:
I spent an hour in a London cafe with two female founders who are both in their early 20s and both building things I couldn't have built. Myah is building rebeauty.app, a resale marketplace for unopened beauty products. Victoria is building Ventureship.co.uk, which replaces CV screening with real project work. We ended up talking less about their products and more about the part nobody films: raising in the UK when investors want conviction and proof at the same time, getting told no, finding [...] Here's what we cover:
How UK and US investors evaluate the exact same pitch differently
Why the UK female founder ecosystem is growing faster than its funding
How both of them found their first customers by physically going outside and talking to strangers
The headache problem vs migraine problem test for whether your idea is worth building
Investor horror stories, including one that made me put my coffee down [...] [10:43] Are you two both hiring right now? Since we're talking about like the job market not being so well and we're we're all founders, so we solve our own employment

results.title: London ranked second best startup hub in the world for tech
results.snippet:
Russ Shaw, Founder of Tech London Advocates, said: "It's particularly impressive to see how high London ranks with reference to early-stage investment - I hope that this sends a distinct message to aspiring tech entrepreneurs that the capital is the number one destination to start their business." [...] London also ranked among the highest for access to early-stage funding, while the capital beat New York on the report's 'connectedness' metric, the ability for a startup to increase its global reach.

However, London lagged behind the Big Apple on 'performance' – the economic impact of the ecosystem and the growth of investor exits from startups.
